decisions.reason: The right-coset definition is sound, but the left-coset remark used the same representative twice. Equality xt_alpha H=t_(x alpha) H gives t_(x alpha)^(-1)xt_alpha in H. Corrected that factor and declared the coset-equality supplier already used in the Definition; the Definition itself is unchanged.

Euclid's prime-product implication is not in either old arithmetic supplier. Cited the published thm-euclids-lemma with a=|M|, b=|N|; the quotient-order formula then makes MN prime to p. Replaced informal collecting of factors by the two inclusions between the generated subgroup and the finite product of normal subgroups. No group-theoretic claim or choice assumption changes.

The construction exports restriction and values, not integrality. F1 now derives virtual-character status from linear induction of honest characters and the irreducible-character basis, whose coefficients are intertwiner dimensions. The norm calculation gives sum n_i^2=1, and positive degree eliminates the negative sign. The restriction identity follows by subtracting d1_H from the constructed extension. Statement unchanged.

The title omitted the contradictory hypothesis Q nontrivial; the Statement correctly concludes Q=1. Renamed the title to that conclusion. The cycle formula gives V(q)=phi(q)^[K:Q]; the prime-to-p power map on the finite abelian p-group is bijective, now explicitly proving the claimed surjectivity. Idempotence of O^p then contradicts nontrivial transfer. Flavell 5.10, pp.14-15, was read and uses this contradiction.

For fixed P of order two, Q nontrivial and Q<=P forces Q=P. Its normalizer is P because a normalizing permutation preserves the two letters of its transposition. The three choices of P are conjugate, so they form one class, not three classes. Corrected assertion 2 and step 2.1; A3 remains the normal complement, and the two-element Sylow controls its own element fusion.

F6 reversed the implication in strong induction and is corrected. The actual proof already uses the correct smaller-order hypothesis: either a central element outside S normalizes S, or Z(P)<=S and the proper quotient subgroup S/Z(P) is properly normalized in the strictly smaller p-group P/Z(P). Lifting the normalizing coset yields x outside S. No Statement change.

The final equivalence was false. In S4 a Sylow D8 is self-normalizing: a larger normalizer would be S4, but its central double transposition has conjugates that are not central in D8. Thus the two control conditions coincide there and both fail. Replaced the false equivalence with the valid inclusion implication and the self-normalizing case. The defining element-fusion quantifier and conjugation convention are retained.

The support rectangle in step 1.1 had its coordinates reversed. For F(x,y)=f(y)g(y^-1 x), y lies in supp f and x lies in (supp f)(supp g); their correctly ordered product is compact and closed. The kernel lemma gives continuity of convolution. For fixed x the associativity kernel is supported where y lies in supp f and z lies in (supp f)(supp g), licensing interchange and z=yw. Statement unchanged.

The pointwise convolution definition does not export continuity. Added the C_c closure lemma as a direct dependency and cited it in F1, with its AC assumption already present. The nonnegative absolute-value kernel is compactly supported in (supp f supp g) x supp f; interchange and left invariance give the product of L1 norms. No sigma-finiteness or global Tonelli assumption is needed.

Outer regularity identifies an infimum of measures, but need not give finite measure of the excess of an open superset when E has infinite measure. Replaced that assertion with the exact infimum transported by right translation. F2 now proves Borel measurability for arbitrary topological spaces from the generated sigma-algebra definition. Compact finiteness, open inner regularity and left invariance then make the pushforward left Haar; uniqueness supplies its positive scalar.

F7's Euclidean citation did not cover arbitrary LCH groups; it now proves Borel measurability by the preimage sigma-algebra argument. Also closed the Borel-density gap: dyadic bands with summable errors prove outer regularity of w mu, and open level-set approximations prove open inner regularity. RMK uniqueness now identifies sigma with that density on all Borel sets. Right invariance, the involution Phi^2=1 and positivity force the scalar to one. Statement unchanged.

F2 omitted Haar regularity, and nonzero compact finiteness alone does not imply it on arbitrary LCH spaces. Here G is an open Euclidean half-plane with a countable rational-rectangle base. Added the compact-finite second-countable regularity corollary under the already assumed AC. The left Jacobian a0^2 cancels the density change, while the right Jacobian a0 gives c(g)=a0 and Delta(g)=a0^-1. Example unchanged.

The carrier explicitly attributes the support bound to the cited proof's construction. In lem-lch-urysohn-cutoff-for-a-compact-set-inside-an-open-set, steps 1.1-2.1 choose V with compact closure contained in U and extend by zero, explicitly yielding support in closure V subset U. This proves the stronger bound needed here. The witness equals one on a positive-area rectangle with a>1, so integral (a-1)f a^-2 is strictly positive. No edit needed.

Unitarity bounds coefficients but does not make an abstract group homomorphism continuous. Made the intended topological-representation convention explicit in the Example, Given and F8. Under continuity the coefficients and averaged rank-one operator are integrable. The intertwiner argument gives zero for inequivalent representations; in the equivalent case the trace is <u,Tz>, and changing a unitary intertwiner by a phase cancels between the two factors.

The remark incorrectly asserted non-eventual-constancy without excluding discrete groups. For U={e}, nonnegative unit mass forces e_U=mu({e})^-1 1_{e}, and every later term is identical. Corrected the remark and the F5 closure citation. The cutoff proof supplies support inside U; compact-kernel integration gives left convergence, density extends it to L1, and the isometric involution gives right convergence. AC supplies the simultaneous choice of cutoffs.

The cited Hilbert-space convention includes strong continuity; the old restatement omitted it and deferred its justification. Restored that requirement and applied the earlier translation-continuity lemma at p=2 to the identical lambda and rho formulas. The modular factor cancels right-translation scaling in the squared norm, and the group laws give inverse unitary operators. Kowalski Proposition 5.2.6 was read; its right-Haar convention differs, so the local left-Haar proof controls the normalization.

F3 used C_c closure absent from the cited definition; added the closure lemma under the existing AC premise. Fatou now explicitly identifies the uniform limit of u_n*f with its L1 limit. A continuous a.e.-zero function vanishes everywhere by positivity on open sets. In a nondiscrete group mu({e})=0; a cutoff supported in a neighbourhood with integral |u|<1 contradicts evaluation at e. Counting measure gives the unit in the discrete case.
